UnitStatement: DOMAIN_DECOMP composes one INIT-TASK brief per dispatch unit using the domain-source-atomize dispatch schema.
A domain-source-atomize brief must identify its purpose, requester, acting surface, scope path, task skill, allowed write targets, runtime overrides, custom instructions, and expected outputs.
RuntimeOverrides in the brief must include source identity, dispatch unit, source paths, line range, skeleton, asset manifest, outputs, and target section IDs.
CustomInstructions in the brief must enforce line-range discipline for atom evidence lines.
Every emitted atom must map to one TARGET_SECTION_IDS entry in its SectionID column.
LocalSeq is monotonic within the dispatch unit and final stable IDs are assigned by the merge step.
ContentHash must be sha1(UnitStatement)[:12] and is load-bearing for deduplication and HTML cross-reference.
SOURCE_REF_MODE=COMPONENT_MAP requires ASSET_MANIFEST_PATH source_components to map generated evidence lines back to original repo component lines.
If SOURCE_REF_BASE is present, workers replace L#### with the source line and <SectionID> with the mapped section.
Without SOURCE_REF_BASE, SourceRef uses the default <book>.md:L####|<book>.html#anchor form.
InOutStatus is restricted to IN, OUT, or TBD.
The default atom status is IN for substantive technical statements.
Boilerplate should be classified OUT.
Ambiguous content should be classified TBD.
The no-invention rule requires workers not to invent facts.
Workers must write only to OUTPUT_LEDGER_PATH and OUTPUT_VOCAB_SEED_PATH.
SOURCE_NAME is the source document stem runtime override.
SOURCE_PREFIX is the downstream ID-assignment prefix runtime override.
DISPATCH_UNIT_ID identifies the dispatch unit in the dispatch plan.
MD_PATH points to the assembled source markdown.
LINE_START and LINE_END define an inclusive assigned line range.
TARGET_SECTION_IDS lists section IDs, and every atom must map to one of them.
SKELETON_PATH points to the source skeleton JSON.
ASSET_MANIFEST_PATH points to the asset manifest JSON.
OUTPUT_LEDGER_PATH is the per-unit atom CSV destination.
OUTPUT_VOCAB_SEED_PATH is the per-unit vocabulary seed CSV destination.
MAX_ATOMS can bound smoke-test atomization and halt processing when reached.
SOURCE_HTML_PATH is included in dual SourceRefs when known.
SOURCE_REF_BASE is a manifest-backed dual-citation template containing L#### and <SectionID> placeholders.
SOURCE_REF_MODE=COMPONENT_MAP is valid when the asset manifest contains source_components line maps.
AllowedWriteTargets must name exactly OUTPUT_LEDGER_PATH and OUTPUT_VOCAB_SEED_PATH.
AllowedWriteTargets is the TASK-shell write-quarantine seal.
The skill cannot write outside AllowedWriteTargets.
CustomInstructions reinforce run-specific constraints but do not replace SKILL.md hydration.
SKILL.md remains the authoritative contract for domain-source-atomize.
The brief builder includes one-line reminders for line range, target section, ContentHash, SourceRef, status enum, no invention, and write boundary.
The orchestrator may add one or two run-specific reminders for recurrent worker errors.
Run-specific reminders should not duplicate the skill contract.
tools/decomp/build_atomization_brief.py renders a valid INIT-TASK brief from a dispatch plan and unit_id.
tools/decomp/build_atomization_brief.py is the deterministic source of truth for brief shape.
Hand-composed domain-source-atomize briefs should be reserved for emergencies.
The orchestrator pipes the brief-builder stdout into the TASK dispatch surface.
A successful run must leave exactly OUTPUT_LEDGER_PATH and OUTPUT_VOCAB_SEED_PATH present.
No file outside the declared write boundary may be created or modified.
The atom CSV header must exactly match the required nine-column header.
The atom CSV must be UTF-8 with columns present in the required order and no extras.
LocalSeq must be strictly increasing positive integers starting at 1 with no gaps or duplicates.
UnitStatement must be non-empty, one concept per row, and preferably no more than about 50 words.
SourceRef must be non-empty and dual-cited.
Manifest-backed SourceRefs are valid in @repo/<RepoRelPath>:L####|source_review_html#SectionID form when SOURCE_REF_BASE is supplied.
Grouped component-map SourceRefs are valid when SOURCE_REF_MODE=COMPONENT_MAP.
In component-map mode, the generated evidence line must fall within the assigned line range.
In component-map mode, the cited repo component line must be derived from source_components.
ContentHash must be non-empty, exactly 12 lowercase hex characters, and equal sha1(UnitStatement)[:12].
InOutStatus must be one of IN, OUT, or TBD.
SectionID must be a member of TARGET_SECTION_IDS.
DispatchUnitID must equal DISPATCH_UNIT_ID.
Corrects must be empty or a semicolon-separated list of HBA-<PREFIX>-NNNNN IDs.
Notes is optional free-form content.
Bare page numbers, isolated headings, navigational markers, copyright statements, dedications, and boilerplate must not be emitted as IN rows.
TBD is reserved for content requiring Gate 2 judgement and is not a catch-all classification.
A slice with zero IN atoms is valid and reports RUN_STATUS=NO_FINDINGS.
For NO_FINDINGS, the atom CSV is header-only and the vocab CSV is still written.
The merge tool re-derives ContentHash and fails the merge on mismatch.
Identical UnitStatement text must always produce the same ContentHash.
The vocab seed CSV header must exactly be CandidateTerm,Synonyms,Definition,SourceRefs,Notes.
The vocab seed CSV must be UTF-8 with the required columns in order and no extras.
CandidateTerm in vocab rows must be non-empty and case-preserved.
Synonyms in vocab rows must be empty or semicolon-separated.
Definition in vocab rows must be empty or an explicit single definition extracted from the source.
SourceRefs in vocab rows must be non-empty and semicolon-separated.
The vocab CSV may be header-only when the slice contains no candidate canonical terms.
RUN_STATUS values are SUCCESS, NO_FINDINGS, FAILED_INPUTS, and FAILED.
The worker reports DISPATCH_UNIT_ID, ATOM_COUNT, IN_COUNT, OUT_COUNT, TBD_COUNT, and VOCAB_COUNT.
Missing or mismatched ContentHash blocks the per-source merge step.
Non-monotonic LocalSeq blocks the per-source merge step.
SectionID outside TARGET_SECTION_IDS blocks the per-source merge step.
A SourceRef outside the assigned line range or not derivable from source_components blocks merge.
An empty UnitStatement on an IN row blocks merge.
Boilerplate emitted as IN blocks merge.
A worker-written final stable AtomicUnitID blocks merge.
Worker stdout and RUN_STATUS are sufficient evidence for routine success.
FAILED and FAILED_INPUTS runs require an explanatory RUN_STATUS evidence note.
domain-source-atomize reads one assigned source markdown slice and emits an atomic-unit ledger and vocabulary seed CSV.
The atomic-unit ledger has one row per atomic unit with LocalSeq, SourceRef, ContentHash, status, and SectionID.
The vocabulary seed CSV records candidate canonical terms with source attribution.
domain-source-atomize is bounded extraction, not whole-source analysis.
One invocation processes one dispatch unit and writes exactly two artifacts.
Cross-source reconciliation, ID assignment, and gate decisions are handled by the orchestrator, not this skill.
The suitable agent shell for domain-source-atomize is TASK in generic shell mode spawned by DOMAIN_DECOMP.
Whole-book atomization should be handled through multiple orchestrator dispatches, not one domain-source-atomize invocation.
Cross-source vocabulary reconciliation belongs to the orchestrator and merge_vocabulary_seeds.py.
Final stable ID assignment belongs to merge_source_atomizations.py.
IN/OUT ratification across multiple sources belongs to the Gate 2 persona.
Required overrides include SOURCE_NAME, SOURCE_PREFIX, DISPATCH_UNIT_ID, MD_PATH, line range, target sections, skeleton, asset manifest, and output paths.
SOURCE_HTML_PATH, SOURCE_REF_BASE, SOURCE_REF_MODE, and MAX_ATOMS are optional runtime overrides.
Read access is limited to the assigned MD_PATH line range, the full skeleton, and the full asset manifest.
The worker must not read other source files, other source markdown, v1.1 archive, prior decomposition ledgers, or cross-source artifacts.
Writes are limited to OUTPUT_LEDGER_PATH and OUTPUT_VOCAB_SEED_PATH.
Parent directories must already exist because domain-source-atomize does not create directories.
No deterministic tools are invoked inside domain-source-atomize.
The allowed-tools frontmatter field is intentionally omitted for domain-source-atomize.
domain-source-atomize must not perform sub-agent fanout.
domain-source-atomize must not perform cross-source reconciliation.
SourceRef supports default handbook, manifest-backed, and grouped component-map citation forms.
Asset-derived atoms anchor to per-kind asset review surfaces; prose-derived atoms anchor to source HTML by default.
AtomicUnitID is not a per-unit CSV column because stable IDs are assigned by the merge tool.
Vocab SourceRefs should list semicolon-separated dual citations where the term appears.
Input validation must confirm required files exist, the line range is valid, target sections exist, and output parents exist.
Invalid inputs require RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS and header-only CSVs at both output paths.
The worker reads only lines LINE_START..LINE_END of MD_PATH.
The worker filters skeleton sections to TARGET_SECTION_IDS for context.
The worker filters manifest assets by page range derived from section page_first and page_last.
Each meaningful statement is normalized into one short atomic statement.
Atom SectionID is assigned from the target section whose line range covers the statement evidence line.
In COMPONENT_MAP mode, SourceRef maps generated MD evidence lines through source_components to original component file lines.
If SOURCE_REF_BASE is absent, the default SourceRef form is <book>.md:L####|<book>.html#anchor.
ContentHash is computed as sha1(UnitStatement)[:12].
IN status applies to substantive technical claims such as principles, procedures, formulas, rules, standards requirements, and definitions.
OUT status applies to boilerplate, repeated headers, copyright matter, navigation markers, and uninterpreted image-caption-only blocks.
TBD status applies to ambiguous content, unresolved conflicts, or unclear text requiring persona judgment.
Corrects is populated only when the text explicitly says the atom corrects an earlier-source statement.
LocalSeq increments by one for each appended atom row.
MAX_ATOMS, when set, halts atomization after that count and writes accumulated rows.
Vocabulary seeding surfaces repeated or emphasized multi-word noun phrases.
Vocabulary seeding records observed synonyms.
Vocabulary seeding captures definitions only when the source explicitly provides them.
Vocabulary seeds must not invent canonical terms or normalize beyond source-visible wording.
Output CSVs must include header rows, UTF-8 encoding, consistent newlines, and Python csv-module quoting conventions.
Line-range discipline requires generated MD evidence lines to remain within LINE_START..LINE_END.
Target-section discipline requires every emitted atom SectionID to be one of TARGET_SECTION_IDS.
Output-path discipline forbids any write beyond the two configured output paths.
The no-invention constraint requires omitted or TBD handling for facts not present in the assigned slice.
Content-hash discipline requires every ContentHash to equal sha1(UnitStatement)[:12].
LocalSeq discipline requires strictly increasing positive integers starting at 1.
SourceRef must include both a source citation and an HTML anchor.
Exactly two output files must exist after the run.
Every row's SectionID must be in TARGET_SECTION_IDS.
The orchestrator runs build_source_skeleton.py to produce the dispatch plan.
The orchestrator renders structure-mode source HTML for Gate 1.5.
The orchestrator uses build_atomization_brief.py per unit_id to render INIT-TASK briefs.
The orchestrator dispatches one TASK + domain-source-atomize invocation per dispatch unit.
The orchestrator runs merge_source_atomizations.py per-source and cross-source after collecting per-unit CSVs.
The orchestrator runs merge_vocabulary_seeds.py to consolidate vocabulary seeds.
The orchestrator renders atom-review HTML for Gate 2 after merging outputs.
domain-source-atomize follows the same per-item fanout pattern as pdf2md-page and drawing-extract-page.
TOOL_POLICY states that domain-source-atomize has no deterministic worker-side tool to run.
The orchestrator runs decomp and retrieval tools outside the worker.
The TASK-enforced allowed deterministic tool set is none.
Operationally invoked deterministic tools inside the worker are none.
The surrounding pipeline uses build_source_skeleton.py for Phase 1 preparation.
The surrounding pipeline uses render_source_html.py for Phase 1 preparation and Phase 2.5 review surfaces.
The surrounding pipeline uses build_atomization_brief.py in Phase 2 to produce worker briefs.
The surrounding pipeline uses merge_source_atomizations.py in Phase 2 close to consume worker outputs.
The surrounding pipeline uses merge_vocabulary_seeds.py in Phase 2 close to consume vocab seeds.
The surrounding pipeline uses source database and retrieval index builders in Phase 2.5.
The worker uses reasoning to identify atomic units in the assigned slice.
The worker uses reasoning to classify atoms as IN, OUT, or TBD.
The worker uses reasoning to surface vocabulary seed candidates.
The worker uses reasoning to detect explicit cross-source Corrects references.
The worker uses reasoning to resolve SectionID by matching evidence lines to skeleton line ranges.
The worker must compute sha1(UnitStatement)[:12], and downstream merge verifies it.
The worker must not invoke retrieval indexes during Phase 2 atomization.
If a write would violate the boundary, the worker returns RUN_STATUS=FAILED and does not attempt a workaround.
